solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Female and male wearing girl's flares

indicators.note: the girl wears the male, so his letters go inside hers

parts.note: a lass is a girl, mostly in northern English and Scottish usage
he is the male pronoun, standing for a man

explanation.surface: A woman and a man share a girl's pair of flared trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flares' looks like the trousers, but it is a verb: something that flashes flares up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe a light that blazes out suddenly and briefly.

clue.text: I floss badly, resulting in something likely to be extracted

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of I floss come out in a poor, mixed-up order

explanation.surface: A dental confession: poor flossing means a tooth will have to come out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a tooth pulled at the dentist; the definition is a relic dug out of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Remains of ancient life preserved in rock are dug out or quarried by palaeontologists.

clue.text: Admitted a sin

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Someone confessed to a wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To have admitted a point is to have conceded or consented to it.

clue.text: Fanfare about hot nuts — sister's idea

indicators.note: about means the publicity word goes round the other letters

parts.note: hype is showy publicity or fanfare

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of hot are scrambled

parts.note: sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A sibling's notion of publicity about spicy nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fanfare' suggests trumpets, but here it is showy publicity; 'sister's idea' reads as one phrase though the sibling only supplies the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory or proposition put forward for testing is an idea.

clue.text: Stick a group of teachers in a school

definitions.text: group of teachers in a school

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a pole carried in the hand and the employees of an organisation.

clue.text: Resisted work and assumed an attitude

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
to pose is to hold a stance or put on an attitude

explanation.surface: Someone fought back against a job while striking a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: To be opposed to something is to have resisted or stood against it.

clue.text: Group of musicians from Oregon clubs, breaking hearts

parts.note: OR is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Oregon
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

indicators.note: breaking signals the letters of hearts are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A band from Oregon wins a club following and breaks hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' and 'hearts' suggest card suits, but only clubs is abbreviated; hearts is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ensemble of instrumental players is a group of musicians.

clue.text: To the listener, moved over

indicators.note: to the listener means the word is said, giving a sound-alike spelt differently

parts.note: passed means moved by or went beyond

explanation.surface: Someone, to a hearer, seems to have gone across.
explanation.definitionFit: Something over and done with is finished, gone by in time.

clue.text: Aggravated the mood's calmed

indicators.note: aggravated means stirred up or disturbed, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Something irritated has settled someone's temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aggravated' and 'calmed' look like opposites in the surface; the first is just the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To have soothed or settled something ruffled is to have made it even and calm.

clue.text: Girl's hair trouble

parts.note: Di's, with Di a short girl's name
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A young woman is having a bad hair day.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress means anguish or difficulty, a kind of trouble.

clue.text: Hit after heads of state caused fight

indicators.note: after puts the hit piece behind the opening letters
the heads of the words state and caused are their opening letters

parts.note: a rap is a sharp blow or knock

explanation.surface: A blow struck after national leaders provoked a conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is informal for a scuffle or brawl.

clue.text: Ten Across is fantastic for older members of the family

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly imagined, so the letters of the two words are freely reshuffled

explanation.surface: A self-referential note that this very clue is a marvel for elderly relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten Across' looks like a cross-reference to this clue, but its nine letters are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Forebears from earlier generations of a family are its forefathers.

clue.text: Spotted fish fin with tide turning

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of fin and tide are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A diver glimpses a fish's fin as the tide turns.
explanation.definitionFit: To have spotted someone is to have recognised or picked them out.

clue.text: Criminal tries to leave Eastern prison

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the remaining letters are bent into a new order
to leave says the letter for Eastern departs from the word tries

explanation.surface: A crook attempts to break out of a jail in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing E from TRIES leaves TRIS, which 'Criminal' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is British slang for a jail.

clue.text: What woman applying mascara sees — pupils slip-up for example?

definitions.meaning: something that brings discredit, as a pupil's mistake does on the teacher

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a mirror image and something that casts discredit on a person.

clue.text: Just the same new vessel there at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A newly built ship sails out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean in spite of that, used to concede a point but continue anyway.

clue.text: Joy, without envy, oddly, gets promotion

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the joy word wraps the other letters

parts.note: elation is great happiness or joy

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of envy

explanation.surface: A happy person, free of jealousy, earns a step up at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', which would remove letters; in older usage it means outside, so the joy word wraps the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone to a higher rank is advancement, a promotion.

clue.text: Brand perhaps holding on after end of sale's profitable

indicators.note: after puts the comedian piece behind that last letter
end of picks the final letter of the word sale
holding means the comic word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Russell Brand is an example of a comedian, a comic

explanation.surface: A brand name keeps going after the sale ends and makes money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand' looks like a trade name; it is the British comedian Russell Brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something paying its way or making a return is financially sound.

clue.text: Universities restricting growth? These are mythical

indicators.note: restricting means the universities word encloses the growth word

parts.note: unis is short for universities
a corn is a hard growth on the foot

explanation.surface: Colleges are putting a curb on development.
explanation.definitionFit: Horned horse-like beasts of legend are mythical creatures.

clue.text: Great to study expert

parts.note: to consider something is to examine or think about it carefully
able means skilled or competent

explanation.surface: Advice that pondering the work of a specialist is a fine thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something large in amount or extent, as in a great or sizeable sum.

clue.text: Seaside attraction's guards left tools

indicators.note: guards means the pier word surrounds and protects the other letter

parts.note: a pier is a seaside attraction, with the 's giving the plural S

explanation.surface: A seaside pier's security guards leave behind some tools.
explanation.definitionFit: These gripping hand tools are pincers for bending and cutting wire.

clue.text: Fairly beautiful

explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as an adverb meaning quite and an adjective meaning attractive.

clue.text: City's good and bad, ironically

definitions.meaning: a resort city on the French Riviera
said sarcastically, as in 'well, that's lovely', it means unpleasant

explanation.surface: A town is described as both wonderful and awful, with a wink.
explanation.definitionFit: The French resort's name doubles as an everyday word for pleasant, which can be used sarcastically for the opposite.

clue.text: Individual in section decrypted CIA URL

parts.note: a part is a section or portion

indicators.note: decrypting turns code into readable form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a department decodes a web address belonging to the CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular and individual both mean relating to one specific person or thing.

clue.text: See what kilt wee Dougal wears?

definitions.text: See what kilt wee Dougal wears?

indicators.note: wears means the words carry the answer within them, worn inside

explanation.surface: A glance at the fabric of a small Scotsman's kilt.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across kilT WEE Dougal, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough woollen cloth from Scotland is the classic fabric worn in kilts and jackets.

clue.text: Charge put on one form of transport

indicators.note: put on means the charge sits on top of the next piece in this down entry

parts.note: a tax is a charge levied
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fee is added to one way of getting around.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab for hire is a means of getting about.

clue.text: Naval soldier eating fish spread

indicators.note: the marine eats the fish, so it goes inside his letters

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving with a navy
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A sea-going soldier tucking into some fish on a piece of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: This butter substitute is a spread for bread.

clue.text: Foolish in record time

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone is daft to try setting a speed record.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy and lacking sense or skill, much like silly behaviour.

clue.text: Copper twisting on his pillow

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: twisting implies the letters of on and his are turned into another order

explanation.surface: A policeman tosses and turns on his pillow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow is a soft pad for resting on, and so is a cushion.

clue.text: Old soap's colouring finally going unpleasant

indicators.note: finally going says the last letter of the colouring word is dropped

parts.note: dye is a substance used for colouring
nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: A vintage bar of soap's colour fading leaves something ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap' suggests something to wash with, but it is a TV soap opera: Dynasty was a 1980s American series.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1980s American prime-time serial is a classic television soap opera.
